problem_statement: mDNS resolvers, browsers and record queriers stop sending initial queries after a fixed small number of attempts, even when no response has ever been received. As a result, a name that is not answered promptly is only queried a few times and then never again until the cache entry is re-activated. Instead, initial queries should keep being sent while the name is unresolved, using an exponential-backoff interval that grows over time and eventually settles on a long (hour-scale) interval, continuing until a response arrives. (The test exercises this by advancing time across many successive query cycles and verifying that a query is still transmitted at each cycle.)
